items.title: Issue durable BrowserBroker grants and forward delegated bearers so the in-app browser opens in production
items.summary: Build real BrowserBroker grant issuance in the Model Plane: when the gateway starts a user browser session it requests a persisted BrowserGrant (org and owner scoped, canonical host policy, TTL, ZDR flag) and sends the returned grant_id on POST /v1/agent/runs, with the delegated browser bearer forwarded to Quarry and to model-gateway (/v1/browser/runs, /v1/browser/suggest-action). Persist the broker store (in memory today) so a restart does not orphan live sessions, and replace the interim 'session:{id}' grant string used by ai-runs with child grants derived from the session grant. Quarry stays the validator and executor.
items.whyItMatters: Production Quarry requires a grant (it refuses to boot without a validator and answers 403 'browser grant_id is required' on run start), but the gateway's session start sends none, so the user-facing browser, in-app AI runs and MCP browser.observe/act only work against dev-mode Quarry. Every other item in this category is gated on this one, so it is the first thing users and agents would hit.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (hardened page hosting, iab-028/029)
others: Aside (Chromium fork, so the same pattern is inferred, INF)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources record it (Codex); treated as common because Aside is a Chromium fork (INF). For Verevon the matching mechanism is a trusted issuer deciding host authority, which is a prerequisite rather than a reference feature.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex's main process intercepts every guest attach (will-attach-webview): it forces partition, session and preload, deletes allowpopups, disablewebsecurity and nodeintegration, and pre-registers a route token so only known tabs can attach; the renderer cannot widen any of it. The Verevon analogue already exists on the Quarry side: host authority is broker-owned (Quarry overwrites a client's allowed_domains with the grant's canonical list at acquisition and revalidates every step). What is missing is the issuer.

verevonToday.gap: Engine and isolation are ahead of both references, but no code path mints a durable BrowserGrant, the gateway sends no grant or browser bearer, and the broker store is in memory only. Prod-mode Quarry therefore rejects the in-app session itself.

items.approach: Model Plane BrowserBroker (Go, grant.go): add a durable store (Postgres) and an issue endpoint for a user-session grant kind (org and owner scoped, ZDR flag, TTL, bounded canonical domain list). Gateway browser.rs create_session calls the issuer with the delegated browser-audience bearer, passes grant_id on /v1/agent/runs and forwards x-browser-authorization to Quarry and model-gateway. start_ai_run (browser.rs:1235) mints a child grant from the session grant instead of the 'session:{id}' string; sensitive actions keep single-use child grants. Add an integration test that runs the gateway against Quarry in prod mode. Quarry is unchanged except for tests; the Model proposes, Quarry validates and executes.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (BrowserBroker) with Frontend Plane gateway wiring
items.risks: Grant scope creep: keep the canonical bounded host list (max 32) and single-use sensitive child grants. Restart semantics for in-flight sessions. Issuing grants for user sessions must not become a way around the model-initiated cross-domain HITL gate.

alreadyPlanned.where: Acknowledged as unbuilt in a gateway code comment (browser.rs:1258-1262); docs/BROWSER_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md still says COMPLETE and is stale.

items.title: Let users browse freely: a human-session policy plus an omnibox that routes free text to Verevon search
items.summary: Add a human-browsing session mode distinct from agent runs: an idle-timeout lease (reset by user input and frame activity) instead of max_steps 12 and 120 s, and a broker-defined navigation policy that is not a single-host list, so omnibox entries and link clicks under takeover work. Agent-initiated cross-domain navigation keeps the existing cross_domain_navigation HITL gate, and Quarry's egress/SSRF policy stays on. Add hard reload and make reload retry a failed URL. Rewire browser-omnibox.ts so URL-like input navigates and free text opens Verevon search (Quarry /v1/search results, or Ask into chat), with suggestions from the gateway's existing search autocomplete and local web history.
items.whyItMatters: A browser locked to its first host for 120 s is not a browser, and today free text in the address bar becomes a google.com URL that the domain lock then rejects. This is the largest day-one usability gap for people, and it is the part of 'a built-in browser users and AI both use' that users touch first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (navigation commands iab-037; omnibox suggestion service iab-036)
others: Aside (omnibox reuses the browser engine plus an AI mode with attached tabs, aside-browser-product-011)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Navigation controls: 1 of 3 recorded (Codex), table-stakes because Aside is Chromium (INF). Omnibox suggestions: 2 of 3, common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Commands navigateBack, navigateForward, reload and hardReload (ignore cache); the preload captures mouse buttons 3 and 4; reload from an error page retries the original URL. The suggestion service is token based: start(query) streams matches {contents, description, destinationURL, acceptToken, deleteToken}; accept(token) navigates and records; deleteMatch removes a history entry. For Verevon: a gateway suggest call that merges local history, search autocomplete and URL heuristics, and non-URL input goes to Verevon search rather than google.com.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:483-495 (every user session: allowed_domains = first host, max_steps 12, max_runtime_s 120)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:1446 (lease ttl defaults to max_runtime_s or 120 s)

apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:326-345,1397-1412 (in governed mode the broker's domain list overwrites client domains and must equal the live run's domains every step)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/lib.rs:59-77 (canonical_broker_domains rejects an empty or over-32 list, so there is no open-web grant today)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:1146 (omnibox use); back/forward/reload ship, hard reload does not
verevonToday.gap: Back, forward and reload ship, but the user cannot leave the first host or browse past 120 s. Because Quarry's governed mode makes the broker the only source of host authority, the allowlist cannot be extended by the gateway or by Quarry alone; a broker-defined policy mode (or a versioned grant re-issue that Quarry validates) is needed. The omnibox has no suggestions and its search fallback cannot work.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (Quarry): add a human session kind on /v1/agent/runs (or a dedicated session route) with an idle reaper, per-navigation timeline rows tagged source=user, and unchanged egress policy. Model Plane BrowserBroker: add a human-browse grant kind (open public web minus a broker/org denylist, audited, bounded) that Quarry validates in place of the exact domain-list equality; Quarry keeps rejecting agent-initiated cross-domain navigation without HITL approval, and Quarry-owned control mode decides whether an action is human or agent. Frontend gateway/omnibox: hard reload, error-page retry, suggest endpoint combining web-history.ts, the search domain autocomplete and URL heuristics; free text opens Quarry /v1/search results in the tab or sends to chat. Share the idle/absolute TTL machinery with R-t2-03-08 instead of building it twice.
dependencies: Gateway search cache gets org/user key and ZDR gating before it feeds suggestions (baseline gap 9)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (Quarry) with Model Plane broker and Frontend Plane omnibox
items.risks: SSRF and egress abuse (keep private-IP blocks and per-navigation audit), unbounded host growth, cost of long-lived Chromium leases (idle reaping), unforgeable user-versus-agent origin of a navigation. Under ZDR no history or suggestions are stored.

alreadyPlanned.where: Recognised as a known gap in the v-browser-app baseline (gap 3); no dated plan found.

items.title: Co-browsing: the agent acts in the user's visible Quarry session, in its own agent-flagged tab
items.summary: Let a Model Plane browser run attach to the Quarry session the user is looking at (same lease and profile) instead of acquiring its own hidden lease. The grant is bound to that session id, the agent works in a new agent-flagged tab that appears in the tab strip without stealing focus, and the user can reveal any agent tab and take it over using Quarry's existing control-mode arbitration. The Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects.
items.whyItMatters: This is the core of 'a browser users and AI both use'. Today the user and the agent work in two separate browsers that share only a profile id and a start URL, so the user cannot watch, redirect or take over the agent's actual page.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (iab-068, hidden agent tabs)
others: Aside (per-tab agent-control indicator and take-over; shipped in Verevon as C-t2-08-017)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources (Codex); unique as a co-browsing model.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Each agent tab gets a hidden webview host (about:blank until the snapshot URL is known); open-browser-tab is sent with active:false; presentation state decides whether the hidden host stays mounted, and the tab strip shows it without focus change. For Verevon: the AI loop attaches to the user's visible Quarry run (same lease, own tab) and Quarry's control-mode arbitration decides who may act.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent.rs:669-690 (the durable run calls start_run for its own leased session; continuity is profile_id and start_url only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:1235-1245 (ai-run body: grant_id 'session:{id}', profile_id, start_url)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx:39,608 (read-only frame view with pause/resume)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:1230 (takeover control in the Crawl composer browser)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/step_receipts.rs:67-70 (control_mode is persisted by the browser owner so a restart cannot reset a takeover)
verevonToday.gap: The AI run drives a different, hidden Quarry lease. The chat panel can watch frames but cannot reveal or take over the agent's tabs in the user's browser, and there is no agent-tab marker in the tab strip.

items.approach: Model Plane: add an attach mode to execution-core browser_agent (attach_session_id instead of client.start_run at browser_agent.rs:669); BrowserBroker issues a run grant bound to that session id, not a free string. Quarry: tab ownership flag opened_by agent|user in the tab list and timeline, agent steps allowed only on agent-flagged tabs (or the active tab when control_mode is agent), existing 409-during-takeover rule kept. Frontend: agent badge on tabs, new agent tab opens without focus, Reveal and Take over buttons, shared timeline. Keep the plane rule that Quarry executes or rejects every proposed action.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (Quarry) with Model Plane browser_agent and Frontend Plane
items.risks: Concurrency between human and agent inside one session; step and cost budgets versus the idle policy of item 02; grant binding to exactly one session; cross-domain navigation by the agent stays behind HITL.

alreadyPlanned.where: Listed as a known gap (v-browser-app baseline gap 4); no plan found.

items.title: Chat beside the browser: a dockable browser panel bound to the chat run
items.summary: Promote BrowserChrome from the dashboard Crawl composer to a dockable panel inside the chat view (right, bottom, maximised, hidden), bound to the chat run's Quarry session, reusing frame streaming, takeover, approvals and the timeline drawer. Add a floating composer over the page and a 'new chat per tab or keep the chat' rule. The chat live-run panel becomes a compact mode of the same component instead of a separate read-only viewer.
items.whyItMatters: Both reference browsers converge on chat and page side by side. It is where the user watches, takes over and talks to the agent about the visible page in one view; Verevon has the pieces (frames in chat runs, takeover, approvals) but not the surface.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (docked browser with floating composer, iab-033)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 3 sources (Codex, Aside); table-stakes for a chat-plus-browser product.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex hosts the browser as right, bottom, detached or hidden, chosen by a command with a layout-stepping command, and a floating composer posts into the active chat. Aside calls sidePanel.setOptions per tabId with a sessionId, resolves the target session when a tab activates, offers a new-session|keep-session setting, and injects a 'you are a sidecar to this page' framing block on the first tab mention.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatLiveRunPanel.tsx:39,608 (compact read-only frame view)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/app/App.tsx:172

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:402
verevonToday.gap: The interactive browser lives only in the dashboard Crawl composer with no standalone route; the chat panel cannot steer the browser or ask about the visible page in the same view.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: extract BrowserChrome into a layout-agnostic panel component, add dock state (right, bottom, maximised, hidden) persisted per user, bind it to the chat run's Quarry session via the gateway browser domain, and add the new-chat-or-keep-chat rule. Page context reaches the Model Plane only through governed attachments (R-t2-08-05); no direct DOM access from the SPA.
items.risks: Layout complexity on small screens; frame bandwidth when docked next to streaming chat.

items.title: Page context to chat: Quarry hit-test, @tab mentions, selection and region attachments, frame context menu
items.summary: Add a Quarry hit-test endpoint that turns a frame point or region into an element descriptor (AX ref, role, name, nearby text, bbox, crop, tab id, URL, snapshot generation). Build the SPA side: a select mode in BrowserChrome, region and image attachments, and an @tab mention token {sessionId, tabId, title, url, snapshotGeneration} that the gateway re-validates against Quarry fail-closed before use. Attachments are labelled 'from page' for the user before sending and enter the Model as BrowserScraped provenance (screened). A right-click menu over the frame (Ask, Explain, Summarize page, Send to Knowledge, Open in new tab) reuses the same hit-test.
items.whyItMatters: Point at the thing and ask about it is the highest-leverage way for the user and the agent to share a browser, and the element descriptors map straight onto the AX refs that browser.act already uses. It also unblocks on-page annotation (R-t2-08-11).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (@tab mention with fail-closed staleness check, iab-059)
others: Aside (richest selection and region attachment payload, aside-browser-product-017; selection quick actions and context menu)
Codex context menu gating annotate items by page eligibility (iab-049)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Mention token tab-v1 {browserId, tabId, title, url}; on use list the tabs and require an exact match or report 'unavailable'. Selection payload {text | region{elementSummary, previewImage, elements[{selector, tagName, role, text, alt, src, href}]}}, kept per tab and cleared on navigation. Codex also shows page-provided metadata or suggested prompts to the user, labelled, and the model only gets what the user submits. For Verevon: BrowserChrome select mode, the gateway asks Quarry to hit-test the frame point, Quarry returns an AX-ref descriptor plus crop, attached to chat with {sessionId, tabId, url, snapshot generation} and re-validated before any action.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardComposer.tsx:3876 (global composer intentionally does not handle @ mentions)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/browser-session.ts:128 ('dom_select' and 'knowledge_ingest' advertised as default capabilities)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:2578,2700 (capability list advertised by the gateway)

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: hit-test and element-descriptor endpoint on the Quarry session API returning AX ref, role, name, nearby text, bbox and crop, tied to the snapshot generation. Frontend Plane: select mode, region/image attach, @tab mention in the chat composer, frame context menu, and a visible 'from page' label. Model Plane: treat attachments as BrowserScraped provenance and re-validate staleness (tab id, URL, generation) before acting; attachments are ephemeral under ZDR.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane with an Ingestion Plane endpoint
items.risks: Prompt injection via page text (keep provenance screening and the user-visible label); ZDR means attachments must stay ephemeral; stale refs after navigation must fail closed.

items.title: Approval loop for agent browser actions: keyboard-first card with redirect, persisted site rules and attention notifications
items.summary: Extend the existing browser approval gate into a full loop. Model Plane owns the approval schema (risk level, display-friendly params, origin, page URL, persist session|always) and persisted per-user or per-org host rules stored as BrowserBroker policy, never widened through Spaces. The SPA renders a keyboard-first card in chat and in the browser panel (Allow with Mod+Enter, Deny with Esc, and a 'do this instead' text that is delivered to the planner as a redirect, plus 'do not ask again' for non-sensitive categories) and deep-links denials to the setting that caused them. Application Plane emits notifications for approval_requested, question and completed with a link into the run, and suppresses them while the session is visible.
items.whyItMatters: The risk categories and the fail-closed deterministic check are already good; what users feel is a card that only approves or rejects, cannot be answered outside the browser panel, and repeats the same question. Background runs need a reliable way to pull the user back without noise, and 'always' rules cut approval fatigue without widening any ACL.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (approval contract, automation-and-safety-064) for the schema; Aside (aside-agent-control-architecture-076) for the card UX; Aside (aside-agent-control-architecture-059, aside-browser-product-097) for visibility-aware notifications
others: Codex notification routing back to the originating session
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Approval prompts: 2 of 3 sources, common. Attention notifications: 2 of 3, common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Approval request = {kind, connector, tool, params_display[{name, display_name, value}], riskLevel low|high, persist ['session','always'], origin, page_url}. UI choices: Allow, Deny, free text that rejects with 'user asked to do X instead', and 'always' that writes a site rule; denials carry a deep link to the permission setting. Notifications: the UI reports {surfaceId, focused, visible, engaged, sessionId, sequence} on focus changes plus a heartbeat; the backend keeps per-user attention entries with 30 and 60 second TTLs and skips notifying for visible sessions, disabled settings and ephemeral sessions; blocking asks use requireInteraction and open the session on click.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:159-164 (risk labels: login, checkout, posting_form, destructive, cross_domain_navigation, persistent_cookie_use)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:322,2049 (BrowserApprovalCard approve/reject via the orchestration approvals API)

Light grep of apps/Application Plane found no browser approval or run event types (INF)
verevonToday.gap: Missing: session/always persistence tied to broker host rules, redirect-with-instruction, keyboard shortcuts, display-friendly params, resolving an approval outside the browser panel, settings deep links, and browser-run notification events with visibility suppression. Also unreachable end to end until grants are issued (R-t2-08-01).

items.approach: Model Plane: extend the approval record and the planner reply path with params_display, persist and redirect_text; persist 'always' as BrowserBroker policy rules keyed by (user or org, host, category) and keep upload/download/dialog single-use. Frontend Plane: shared approval card used in chat and the browser panel, keyboard shortcuts, settings deep links, and a visibility heartbeat. Application Plane: browser event types on the existing notifications API with cta_href to the run; ZDR or ephemeral sessions send title-only bodies.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (schema and rules) with Frontend Plane and Application Plane
items.risks: Over-broad 'always' rules (keep sensitive categories single-use); notification bodies must not leak page content under ZDR; the notification half is unverified.

items.title: Browser permission policy: per-site agent rules, org policy and a Browser settings hub
items.summary: Create one place where users and admins see and revoke what the agent may do on which sites. Model Plane BrowserBroker gets a policy store with per-origin rules (approval mode, downloads, uploads, cross-domain navigation) in user and org layers. Control Plane owns an org browser policy (site allow and deny lists, persistent approvals allowed or not, recording allowed, ZDR default, profile scopes) that the broker reads when it issues grants, fail-closed and audited. The SPA gets a Settings > Browser section with the rule matrix, managed items labelled, and ZDR and retention shown read-only.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent approvals (item 06) need a visible, revocable home, and enterprise buyers expect admins to constrain agent browsing. Authority already lives server-side in the broker, and the browser is remote, so there is no device-sync problem to solve.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (settings hub with agent-permission matrix, iab-071; synced and admin-managed policy, iab-056/057)
others: Aside (settings hub as web pages covering AI, agents, MCP and privacy)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Settings hub: 2 of 3 sources, table-stakes. Admin-managed synced policy: 1 of 3 (Codex), unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Settings routes under /settings/browser-use/*; an agent-permission matrix lists per-origin rules (approval modes, downloads, uploads, CDP, site tools). Local config tables are projected to a server settings endpoint with revisions and conflicts surfaced; enterprise requirement keys (for example external profile import disabled, global persistent approvals disallowed) are enforced by asserting functions before any write, and managed items are labelled.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/settings/components (no browser section; the only matches are unrelated MCP, account and workspace pages)
apps/Control Plane (light grep: no browser_policy, allowed_sites or blocked_sites symbols)
Broker grants are per grant with host allowlists, not user-editable rules (v-browser-app baseline)
verevonToday.gap: No Browser settings section, no per-site agent-permission matrix, no org-level browser policy. Both are inferred from light greps of the settings feature and the Control Plane, so treat the status as likely, not proven.

items.approach: Control Plane: org browser policy resource with versioned writes and audit; Model Plane BrowserBroker: rule store plus policy evaluation at grant issue time (fail-closed); Frontend Plane: Settings > Browser backed by gateway endpoints that proxy the broker; managed rows labelled and locked. Rules never widen an owner-plane ACL through Spaces.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (org policy), Model Plane (BrowserBroker rules), Frontend Plane (settings)
items.risks: Policy evaluation must be fail-closed and audited; rules must not widen owner ACLs via Spaces; ZDR default has to propagate to grants.

items.title: Capture-time secret redaction of page snapshots and screenshots in Quarry
items.summary: Add a deterministic redaction pass inside Quarry's snapshot and observation builder, before anything is persisted or returned to the Model Plane. Drop values of password and tel inputs and of sensitive autocomplete tokens, scrub fields whose label looks secret (cvv, otp, pin, ssn), and replace secret-shaped values (JWT, AWS access keys, API keys, Slack tokens, private key blocks, numeric OTPs, Luhn-valid 13 to 19 digit card numbers) with [redacted]. Mask those fields in screenshots using their bounding boxes before they are stored or sent to vision.
items.whyItMatters: AX snapshots and screenshots go to Model Plane inference and into evidence storage. Redacting at the executor protects ZDR and non-ZDR tenants alike and limits prompt leakage, particularly with human takeover logins now happening inside the same sessions the agent observes.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: In the accessibility-snapshot capture: drop values for input types password and tel and for sensitive autocomplete tokens; regexes on field labels (cvv, otp, pin, ssn, secret); value patterns (jwt, aws-access-key, api-key, slack-token, private-key-block, labelled secret, numeric OTP) plus a Luhn check for digit runs; replace with [redacted]. Rules are layered and applied before storage.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:1053 (redact_egress_url redacts egress URLs only)
Light grep of apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates found no input-type, secret-pattern or Luhn redaction outside a test site (INF)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent.rs (no password, secret or redact matches)
verevonToday.gap: Only URLs and egress receipts are redacted. No value-level redaction of AX snapshots, DOM observations or screenshots was found; the snapshot builder was not read end to end, so confirm before building.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser snapshot and observation builder): a rule module with unit tests that run before persistence and before the response to the Model Plane; screenshot masking of password-like fields using their rects; keep rules auditable and versioned. Confirm separately whether typed text for sensitive fields appears in action receipts. Reuse rule definitions with R-t2-02-09 (PII stage for scraped content) but keep this pass deterministic and local to live observation.
items.risks: False positives hide useful values (keep rules auditable); regex cost on large snapshots; screenshot masking depends on accurate rects.

items.title: Downloads into quarantined, tenant-scoped artifacts with a downloads drawer and agent-aware gating
items.summary: Turn on downloads in the Chromiumoxide driver: route downloads to a per-session quarantine directory and register the result as a tenant-scoped Quarry artifact (size and type limits, hash, malware-scan hook), withheld under ZDR. User-initiated downloads under takeover are allowed; agent downloads need the existing single-use sensitive download_ref child grant, and unsolicited downloads are cancelled. Emit started, in_progress, complete, failed and canceled events into the timeline, and add a downloads drawer in BrowserChrome with 'Save to Knowledge'.
items.whyItMatters: Agents and users need to fetch PDFs and exports into Knowledge, and the authority model already exists in the contracts and the broker. Without it any page that serves a file is a dead end.

others: Aside (download bubble and dangerous-download blocking, aside-browser-product-024)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources record it as a gated manager (Codex); Aside has a standard download bubble. Unique as an agent-aware gate.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: will-download handler: cancel unless the download is user-initiated or matches a consumed agent grant (consumeAllowedBrowserUseDownload); a status machine started, in_progress, paused, complete, failed, canceled is pushed to the agent. Verevon: download_ref already requires a single-use sensitive child grant; files become tenant-scoped Quarry artifacts listed in a downloads drawer.

items.title: Persist and restore a run's tab set with a live-page budget (task-scoped tabs)
items.summary: Extend Quarry's existing AgentRunCheckpoint, which today stores one current_url, page hash, constraints, viewport, zdr, grant id and control mode, with the full tab list (URL, title, a bounded history window, active tab, agent or user flag). Resume then means a new lease plus lazy tab restore, and reopening a chat thread shows its tabs. Add a live-page budget in the lease scheduler that protects the active, agent-controlled, loading and downloading tabs and evicts by inactivity, restoring from the checkpoint on demand. Nothing is persisted under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: A paused agent run or a HITL handoff can resume on the same pages, and idle Chromium pages stop costing money. It is also what makes co-browsing durable across a closed laptop.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (iab-034 thread-keyed tabs, iab-035 history snapshots, iab-031 live-page budget)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources (Codex); unique as a complete lifecycle.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Key pages by (conversationId, tabId). Persist {navigation:{currentIndex, entries[{url, title, pageState}]}, favicon, title}. Budget: at most N (32) live pages; protect active, agent-controlled, audible, capturing, loading and downloading tabs; evict by inactivity rank; restore lazily by recreating the page and replaying history.

items.title: Frame overlay layer: agent cursor and target highlight, plus real on-page annotation markers
items.summary: Build one overlay layer in BrowserChrome that maps Quarry AX-ref rects (scaled to the frame) onto the frame stream. Use it for (a) an agent cursor and element highlight driven by the target rect that Quarry includes in the pre-action event, without blocking execution on a UI acknowledgement, and (b) an annotation mode where the user marks an element, text or region and the markers stay anchored to AX refs; a batch is sent to chat as one message carrying role, name, ref or selector, rect, nearby text, frame path and an optional screenshot. As an immediate small step, stop advertising the 'annotate' capability and remove the hard-coded placeholder anchor until this is real.
items.whyItMatters: It makes agent actions legible and trustworthy during co-browsing, gives users a precise way to tell the agent what to change or extract, and removes a visibly fake feature: the gateway advertises annotate while the UI shows one fixed marker.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (annotation iab-060/061; agent cursor automation-and-safety-063)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Cursor: moveMouse assigns a sequence number, pushes {moveSequence, x, y} to the host overlay, and waits for a cursor-arrived ack (timeout 1500 ms) before dispatching the click. Annotation: comment payload {pageUrl, framePath, selectedText or targetDescription, targetRole, targetName, targetSelector, targetPath, targetRect, nearbyText, additionalSelections, marker point, screenshot}; overlay modes browse and comment; batch mode collects several comments before sending. Verevon: Quarry emits the target point from the AX-ref bbox before executing and may wait a short fixed delay instead of an ack.

items.title: Browser chrome polish in the SPA: tab menu, new-tab page, typed error cards, split view, keyboard commands, activity strip, reader view
items.summary: A bundle of Frontend-led refinements that need little or no new Quarry surface. Tab context menu with duplicate (new tab, same URL and profile), reopen-closed (a closed-tab stack in Quarry session state), reorder, copy URL and open in the system browser. A new tab renders a compact search-or-ask page built from DashboardSearchPanel and the composer. Quarry returns typed navigation errors (network error, egress-policy denial, domain-lock denial, anti-bot) and BrowserChrome shows a Norwegian-first error card with retry and the reason. Register browser commands in the app's shortcut registry (without stealing keys forwarded to the remote page during takeover). Optional later: split view of two Quarry tab streams, a low-rate multi-run activity strip, and a reader view from the Quarry scrape markdown (translation through Model Plane inference outside ZDR).
items.whyItMatters: Removes small daily frictions once the browser is usable (items 01 to 04) and makes denials and failures understandable instead of silent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (tab menu commands, error pages, top sites, central keymap, browser activity preview)
others: Aside (search-or-ask new tab page, split view, tab-capture live previews, reader mode)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Tab operations: 1 of 3 recorded (table-stakes by inference). New tab page and live previews: 2 of 3, common. Error pages, split view, keyboard commands, reader/translation: 1 of 3, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tab context-menu command ids (copyUrl, duplicate, newTabToTheRight, rename, reload, openInExternalBrowser) dispatch to a tab store and duplicate clones history; on load failure net error codes map to localized categories and a local error document is rendered with the original URL stored so reload retries it; accelerators are named commands in a central keymap. Aside paints the new-tab omnibox immediately and mounts the composer in ask mode. Preview: thumbnail of each active run's latest frame, click to open the full panel.

items.title: Browsing data lifecycle: server-side history with agent/user source, bookmarks, clear-site-data, permission-deny events, support export
items.summary: Derive a per-user visit log from Quarry session timelines, tagged source agent|user, retention-limited and disabled under ZDR, and show it in a history page with an agent filter and a short list of user-scoped bookmarks (or reuse Knowledge saved sources). Add clear-site-data on a profile by type and origin (cookies, storage, cache) with counts first. Make permission handling deny-by-default in the driver with a 'permission requested' event shown as an info chip. Add an opt-in, redacted export of a session's timeline and receipts to support tickets, never under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: History and clear-data are table-stakes in both reference browsers and let users see and undo what the agent did in their profile; Verevon today only keeps a browser-local list of 10 entries. Category 1 deferred a consent-gated history query for agents to this item, so it also prepares a bounded read tool.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (history with Agent badge and source filter; clear-browsing-data dialog with counts; prompts keyed per page)
others: Aside (bookmarks, history panel, downloads bubble, privacy page)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: History and bookmarks: 2 of 3 sources, table-stakes. Clear data: 2 of 3, table-stakes. Permission prompts and diagnostics: 1 of 3 each, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: History store deduplicated by day with favicons; each visit tagged agent|user; a settings page with search, delete-selected and a source filter; agent-facing history reads are gated by their own approval mode. Clear dialog maps selected data types and range to storage clears and shows counts first. Permissions: default deny for request and check handlers with a prompt store keyed per page. Diagnostics: opt-in tab diagnostics attachment and a bounded ring buffer of recent session events.

dropped.reason: Draft-preview cards for outgoing messages belong to provider-action approvals in integration-corev2 (Integration Plane), not the browser shell; revisit in that category.

Duplicate of R-t2-03-08, which already proposes optional recording gated by org policy and off under ZDR; the leftover UI is an HLS player in BrowserTimelineDetail.tsx to add when that lands. Receipt replay is the lighter, more auditable default.

Ad and tracker blocking is Quarry request interception owned by the rendering and anti-bot categories (Firecrawl-style blockAds); no shell-specific work, and it risks site breakage and anti-bot detection.

No evidence of HTTP preview endpoints in Model Plane sandboxes (grep found none); Verevon's browser is remote, so localhost port-forwarding has no analogue and a scoped egress exception to internal hosts is a security risk. Revisit if sandboxes publish previews.

Exposing browser.observe/act to external agents (CLI, skill and MCP install) overlaps R-t2-01-11 (external contract: OpenAPI, MCP server, SDK, CLI/skills) and needs customer API keys; build it there once R-t2-08-01 grants exist.

strengthsToKeep: Remote isolation: the page runs in a leased Chromium inside Quarry and the SPA only receives frames and sends typed input, so nothing executes on the user's machine or in the SPA origin; stronger than Codex's and Aside's local embedding (apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs; apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:180; apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:1600,1730). Keep this contract when adding docking, free browsing and co-browsing.

Host authority is broker-owned and revalidated: Quarry overwrites client allowed_domains with the broker's canonical list and rechecks it every step, and download, upload and dialog actions need a single-use parent grant (apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:157,202,249,306-345,1397-1412; quarry-browser/src/lib.rs:59-77). Neither reference has an equivalent server-side authority; extend it, do not bypass it.

Take-over authority lives in Quarry: control_mode is persisted by the browser owner so a gateway restart cannot reset a human takeover, and agent actions are refused during takeover (apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-runtime/src/step_receipts.rs:67-70; comparator cluster C-t2-08-017).

Profiles and Zero-Data-Retention are better governed than either reference's incognito mode: scoped profiles with restore probe, persistent profiles refused under ZDR, artifacts withheld, vision summary skipped, local web history purged and run checkpoints refused (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:470-474; apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:1181,1245; apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-edge/src/agent_routes.rs:1436-1441).

Approval gate with named risk categories and a deterministic fail-closed backstop, reusing the durable Approval record instead of a parallel system (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:159-164,322; apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/browser_agent.rs:220-240).

Timeline and evidence drawer with receipt replay and a DevTools drawer that includes network and vision views: lighter and more auditable than video or a plain transcript (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:1912-1940,2090-2121; BrowserTimelineDetail.tsx).

Egress is policed at the driver (per-session proxy plus CDP Fetch boundary) and egress receipts are redacted before they leave the driver (apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/crates/quarry-browser/src/chromiumoxide.rs:1053,1877-1890).
